Greek diplomatic sources have said that Libya's latest protest over Greek hydrocarbon surveys is not a new note but an August one restating Tripoli's standing positions, after reports that Libya had threatened to halt bilateral talks.
The note challenges Greek exploration and warns Tripoli could suspend negotiations, according to Greek media.

Τουρκία: Στο επίκεντρο το καλώδιο Ελλάδας και Κύπρου - Το Anadolu επαναφέρει την προειδοποίηση της Άγκυρας
Η είδηση μεταδόθηκε αργά το βράδυ της Τετάρτης.
"Ή σταματάτε τις έρευνες ή παγώνουν οι συνομιλίες". Αυτό είναι το μήνυμα που, σύμφωνα με την τουρκική εφημερίδα Aydınlık, στέλνει η Λιβύη στην Ελλάδα για τις ενεργειακές έρευνες νότια της Κρήτης.

Greece has vowed to take "all appropriate measures" to defend its sovereign rights after Libya's parliament ratified a contested maritime boundary deal with Turkey.
The move reopens one of the eastern Mediterranean's most combustible disputes and hands Ankara a significant diplomatic win.

Greece has raised the eastern Libyan parliament's ratification of a contested maritime deal with Turkey at the U.N. Security Council, warning that it threatens security and stability in the eastern Mediterranean.
Greece's U.N. ambassador, Aglaia Balta, briefed the council during closed consultations on the instructions of Foreign Minister Giorgos Gerapetritis, diplomatic sources said.

Greece and Egypt have agreed to resume talks on extending their 2020 maritime boundary agreement.
It is the first joint diplomatic response to the ratification of a rival Turkey-Libya deal that both countries reject.
Negotiations that had stalled for years will now focus on waters east of the 28th meridian, where the 2020 line ends.

The State Department has called the ratification of a contested maritime pact between Turkey and Libya "provocative."
It is Washington's bluntest criticism yet of a deal that has inflamed tensions in the eastern Mediterranean.

Greece has used its turn at the helm of the United Nations Security Council to rally an unusual coalition against Turkey.
The European Union, Cyprus, Egypt and two Persian Gulf monarchies joined Athens in declaring a contested Turkey-Libya maritime pact "null and void."
Foreign Minister Giorgos Gerapetritis of Greece read the joint statement on behalf of Greece, Cyprus, the European Union, Egypt, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates.
